versions.name: Camp Marin-Sierra

features.note: Swimming, lifesaving, a BSA Mile Swim, and a Polar-Bear Swim.
An aquatics programme centred on alpine Chubb Lake.
Granite walls, cliffs, and overhangs on the camp's western edge, with routes for all skill levels; the council calls it some of the best summer-camp climbing in Northern California.
Sheer and overhanging rappels of 40 to 80 feet.
An ecology and conservation programme area.
An interfaith chapel service opens the week.
Central dining in the commissary area for most of the week.
A jamboree cooking option, with troops cooking in their own campsites.
A Trail-to-First Class area guiding newer Scouts through rank advancement.
Trail-to-Eagle classes for older Scouts who have earned most camp merit badges.
Backcountry treks of one to three nights in the Tahoe National Forest, before or after a camp week.

versions.summary: Marin Council's Scouts BSA resident summer camp located at Emigrant Gap within the Tahoe National Forest.

provenance.notes: Imported from camp-finder; raw description and sessions dropped (operational data stays at the council site). verified_at is camp-finder's own source-confirmation date; imported_at is when open-scout-api ingested it. The evergreen summary is original prose regenerated from that description, excluding dates/fees/schedules. camp_type classified from program_types. Features surveyed 2026-07-25 against the council's own camp page (that page is explicitly not an exhaustive activity list, so absence of a code is not evidence of absence).
